text:
Ethan Morales: Hey, small issue — my Day 1 invite shows twice with different timezones. One says 08:00 PDT, the other 16:00 CET. I only need the local one.
Priya Singh: Hi @Ethan! We're aware. The calendar exporter currently emits a floating event plus a region-specific instance for some cohorts. Keep the one labeled '(local)'.
Ethan Morales: Where do I see that label? My client truncates event titles on mobile.
Hannah Lewis: On mobile open the event details > look at the event description line right under the title. We put '(local)' at the end of the summary and also add a short note in the description: "Use event with suffix (local)".
Ethan Morales: Awesome, thanks. Also the invite mentions recordings but no link — will the recording be attached to the event later?
Onboard Bot: @channel Recording flow: Zoom cloud recording -> processing -> copied to onboarding S3 -> short-lived presigned link posted in this thread (posted within ~30m) -> archived to Onboarding Drive/Notion within 48h.
Priya Singh: If you don't have Drive access, we post the Notion view link which is team-visible. Presigned links expire in 7 days.
Ethan Morales: If the presigned link expires before I can watch, any longer-term option?
Calendar Team: We keep an archive in the onboarding Drive and Notion. If you need longer access sooner, file a quick IT ticket with reason and we'll extend a specific pre-signed URL for 14 days.
Ethan Morales: One last thing: I clicked the Zoom cloud link and it asked for a passcode. How do I get it?
Zoom Bot: Automated note: Some Zoom cloud recordings retain passcode protection. We strip passcodes when copying to S3, but a small subset requires a passcode on the original cloud link. Reply in-thread and Calendar Team will provide a temporary passcode or direct S3 link.
Ethan Morales: OK will do. Thanks all! :pray:
Priya Singh: We'll also push a small ICS fix today to remove the duplicate floating event. Will update this thread when deployed.
